heroBody: The Shen Foundation champions Asian diasporic artists as important makers in our time, cultivating a generative environment where bold ideas, experimental practices, and challenging projects can take form and circulate widely. It forges enduring relationships with artists grounded in trust, rigor, and curiosity, creating conditions in which new artistic languages, risks, and contradictions are supported and understood.

intro.title: What we do
intro.body: REWRITE We organize special temporary exhibitions and new commissions, working closely with artists to bring ambitious, large-scale projects into being. This work is built on trust, patience and long-term relationships — commissioning contemporary art takes time, and we're committed to doing it right.

people.name: Eleanor Shen
people.bio: Eleanor Shen is a collector, philanthropist, and founder of The Shen Foundation, who has championed contemporary art and artists for more than two decades. Her patronage spans museums, galleries, and biennials in Canada and abroad. Since 2014, she has devoted much of her collecting and philanthropy to artists of Asian heritage and the Asian diaspora, advancing their recognition and representation within major art institutions. This commitment lies at the heart of the foundation. Shen has served on the Board of Trustees of the Art Gallery of Ontario since 2015 and is currently a member of its Collections and People Committees. Internationally, she serves on multiple acquisition committees at Tate Modern and the Centre Pompidou. Through her advocacy and support, she has helped bring works by Asian and Asian diasporic artists into the permanent collections of all three museums. She is also a member of the New Museum’s International Leadership Council. Her previous leadership roles include board positions at The Power Plant Contemporary Art Gallery, the Canadian Art Foundation, and Soulpepper Theatre Company, as well as serving as co-chair of Partners in Art.

people.name: Kitty Scott
people.bio: Kitty Scott is Director and Curator of The Shen Foundation. She is a leading curator and writer whose work spans major art institutions and major international exhibitions. She is known for shaping contemporary art discourse through ambitious programming and sustained collaborations with artists. Scott has held key curatorial posts including Curator of Contemporary Art and later Deputy Director and Chief Curator at the National Gallery of Canada in Ottawa. She also served as the Carol and Morton Rapp Curator of Modern and Contemporary Art at the Art Gallery of Ontario in Toronto. Previously, she was Chief Curator at London’s Serpentine Gallery and Director of Visual Arts here at The Banff Centre, where she oversaw residencies, exhibitions and the Banff International Curatorial Institute. Scott was appointed Chief Curator of the 15th Shanghai Biennale, 2025-26, Does the flower hear the Bee? and was a core agent for dOCUMENTA (13) in 2012. With Sally Tallant she co-curated the 2018 Liverpool Biennial, Beautiful world, where are you?. In 2017 she curated Geoffrey Farmer’s exhibition for the Canada Pavilion at the 57th Venice Biennale. Across these roles she has championed a wide range of contemporary artists while publishing extensively in catalogues, books and journals.
